grammar_focus: put 短语(put out/put off/put up with)、except·except for·apart from、dress 与 dress up 的区别、watch 与 follow 的区别、lose one's temper·in the mood for(情绪表达)(原创承载 NCE3 L40 考点·轻净化:恶作剧误会喜剧内核保留,把'强行夺钻/激烈扭打'措辞放缓成'争执/试图拿走';美式化 jackhammer/fire department/police officer)
scene: 大学生为什么似乎比谁都爱搞恶作剧,这一直没人说得清。学生们尤其擅长一种恶作剧:骗局。请消防队来扑灭一场根本不存在的火,是一种拙劣的欺骗,任何一个自重的学生都不屑去做。学生们常常制造一些除了受害者、人人都觉得好笑的场面。前不久,一个学生看见两名工人在校门外用风镐刨路,他立刻打电话报警,说有两个学生假扮成工人在破坏马路。刚一挂断电话,他就走到工人跟前,告诉他们:要是有警察来叫他们走开,千万别当真——因为有个学生扮成了警察,正到处捉弄人。警察和工人都很感激这个学生提前透了风。那学生躲进附近一座拱形门楼,能看清、听清这里发生的一切。果然,一位警察赶到现场,礼貌地请工人离开。当他从一名工人那里得到一句很粗鲁的回话时,便警告说要强制他们停工。工人叫他随便,警察只好打电话求援。不一会儿,又来了四名警察,对工人们规劝告诫。见工人拒不停工,警察便想把风镐拿走。工人们激烈争执起来,其中一个发起了脾气,威胁说要报警。这时,警察讽刺地指出:这大可不必,因为这几个人早已被逮捕了。一名工人装出一本正经的样子,问在被带去警局之前能不能打个电话。警察准了,还陪他去了一部公用电话。直到看见那人真的在给警察打电话,那名警察才恍然大悟:原来他们全都上了这场恶作剧的当。

grammar_card.title: put 短语 / except·apart from / dress vs dress up / watch vs follow / lose one's temper·in the mood
grammar_card.intro: ①put 短语:put out(扑灭)、put off(推迟)、put up with(忍受)、put up(搭起/留宿)。②except / except for “除…之外(不包括)”;apart from 常用于句首。③dress=给…穿衣(dress the baby);dress up=乔装、盛装打扮(dress up as)。④watch=观看、注视;follow=跟随、看懂(思路)。⑤lose one's temper=发脾气;in the mood (for)=有心情(做…);in a good/bad mood=心情好/坏。

funny to everyone except the victims
lose one's temper / in the mood
one of them lost his temper

specialRules.rule: dress the baby=给宝宝穿衣;dress up as=乔装/打扮成。dress 是及物的“给…穿衣”,dress up 才是“乔装、盛装”。
watch 是“观看、注视”;follow 是“跟随”或“看懂、听懂(思路、情节)”:I can't follow the plot。
美式:jackhammer(英式 pneumatic drill)、fire department(英式 fire brigade)、police officer(英式 policeman)、sidewalk(英式 pavement)。本课已按美语写。

prelisten.q: Listen and answer — How did the police officer discover that the whole thing was a joke?
options: He saw the workman actually phoning the real police

passage: It has never been explained why college students seem to enjoy practical jokes more than anyone else. Students specialize in a particular type of practical joke: the hoax. Inviting the fire department to put out a nonexistent fire is a crude form of deception that no self-respecting student would ever indulge in. Students often create amusing situations that are funny to everyone except the victims. When a student recently saw two workmen using a jackhammer outside his college, he immediately telephoned the police and informed them that two students dressed up as workmen were tearing up the road. As soon as he had hung up, he went over to the workmen and told them that if a police officer ordered them to leave, they were not to take him seriously. He added that a student had dressed up as a police officer and was playing all sorts of silly jokes on people. Both the police and the workmen were grateful to the student for this piece of advance information. The student hid in an archway nearby where he could watch and hear everything that went on. Sure enough, a police officer arrived on the scene and politely asked the workmen to leave. When he received a very rude reply from one of the workmen, he warned that he would make them stop. The workmen told him to do as he pleased, and the officer telephoned for help. Shortly afterward, four more officers arrived and remonstrated with the workmen. As the men refused to stop working, the police tried to take away the jackhammer. The workmen argued fiercely, and one of them lost his temper. He threatened to call the police. At this, the officers pointed out ironically that this would hardly be necessary, as the men were already under arrest. Pretending to speak seriously, one of the workmen asked if he might make a telephone call before being taken to the station. Permission was granted, and an officer accompanied him to a pay phone. Only when he saw that the man was actually telephoning the police did the officer realize that they had all been the victims of a hoax.

stage5.stem: "The fire department came to put ___ the fire."("扑灭(火)"用 put ___)
"They had to put ___ the meeting until next week."("推迟"用 put ___)
stage5.stem_cn: 他们只好把会议推迟到下周。

stage5.stem: "I can't put ___ with all this noise."("忍受"用 put ___ with)
"The joke was funny to everyone ___ the victims."("除…之外(不包括)",后接名词/代词)
stage5.stem_cn: 除了受害者,这玩笑人人都觉得好笑。

stage5.stem: "The road was empty ___ for a single truck."(句中用"除…之外"常加 for)
stage5.stem_cn: 路上空荡荡的,只有一辆卡车。

stage5.stem: "___ from the noise, the town was pleasant."(句首"除…之外"用哪个)
stage5.stem_cn: 除了吵,这个镇还挺不错。

stage5.stem: "Two students ___ up as workmen to fool the police."("乔装打扮成"用哪个)
stage5.stem_cn: 两个学生乔装成工人来骗警察。

stage5.stem: "She ___ the baby before breakfast."("给…穿衣服"用哪个)
stage5.stem_cn: 她早饭前给宝宝穿好衣服。

stage5.stem: "The children love to ___ up for parties."("盛装打扮/乔装"用哪个)
stage5.stem_cn: 孩子们喜欢为聚会盛装打扮。

stage5.stem: "He hid in an archway where he could ___ everything."("观看、注视"用哪个)
stage5.stem_cn: 他躲在门楼里,能看清发生的一切。

stage5.stem: "The dog ___ its owner down the street."("跟随、跟着"用哪个)
"I couldn't ___ the plot of the movie."("看懂、理解(情节)"用哪个)
stage5.stem_cn: 我看不懂这部电影的情节。

stage5.stem: "One of the workmen lost his ___."("发脾气":lose one's ___)
"I'm not in the ___ for jokes today."("没心情(做…)":in the ___ for)
"He calmed down and was soon in a better ___."("心情":in a good/better ___)
stage5.stem_cn: 他冷静下来,很快心情就好些了。

stage5.stem: "A trick that fools people into believing something false is a ___."("骗局、戏弄"用哪个词)
stage5.stem_cn: 让人信以为真的恶作剧骗局。

stage5.stem: "To argue and protest in order to warn someone is to ___."("规劝、告诫"用哪个词)
"Saying the opposite of what you mean, often mockingly, is speaking ___."("讽刺地"用哪个词)
stage5.stem_cn: 说反话、带讽刺意味地说。

The joke was funny to everyone beside the victims.

The joke was funny to everyone except of the victims.

stage9_scenario.stem: 你想说"两个学生乔装成工人"(dress up as):
options: Two students dressed up as workmen.
Two students dressed as up workmen.

stage9_scenario.stem: 你想说"有个工人发起了脾气"(lose one's temper):
options: One of the workmen lost his temper.
One of the workmen lost his mood.
One of the workmen lost the temper of him.
One of the workmen lose his temper.
